SCADA Abaran New · Odoo Integration Help

Type: MariaDB Database Connection (Native)

1) Database Connection

Uses mysql-connector-python or pymysql library to connect to SCADA MariaDB database.

Connection Parameters (JSON):

{
  "driver_name": "MariaDB",
  "host": "192.168.1.100",
  "port": 3306,
  "database": "scada_abaran_new",
  "user": "scada_user",
  "password": "password",
  "charset": "utf8mb4"
}

Important Notes:

  • driver_name: Must be "MariaDB" (native connection, NOT ODBC)
  • charset: utf8mb4 for full Unicode support
  • Single database: All devices in one database

2) Database Structure

Each device has its own table in the MariaDB database.

Table Structure:

  • ID_MEDIDA: Auto-increment primary key
  • FECHA_HORA: Timestamp in format DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM (e.g., "19/11/2025 13:45")
  • Sensor columns: CAUDAL, VOLUMEN, PRESION, etc. (varies by device)

Example table: a1_2

ID_MEDIDA | FECHA_HORA       | CAUDAL | VOLUMEN | PRESION
----------+------------------+--------+---------+--------
        1 | 19/11/2025 13:45 |   12.5 |  1250.0 |    2.3
        2 | 19/11/2025 14:00 |   11.8 |  1261.8 |    2.2
        3 | 19/11/2025 14:15 |   13.2 |  1275.0 |    2.4

3) Date Format (AUTO-DETECT)

Supported date formats (auto-detected):

  • ISO Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (e.g., "2026-02-03 15:00:00")
  • ISO with milliseconds: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm (e.g., "2026-02-03 15:00:00.000")
  • Spanish Format: DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM (e.g., "19/11/2025 13:45")
  • Spanish with seconds: DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS (e.g., "19/11/2025 13:45:30")
  • Timezone: Europe/Madrid → Automatically converted to UTC for Odoo
  • NOT configurable: Format is auto-detected from database values

Note: Do NOT include datetime_format in sensor configuration - format is auto-detected

4) Device Configuration

Each mdm.measurement.device requires:

  • Set remotecontrol_id to "SCADA Abaran New"
  • Configure remotecontrol_params (JSON):

Device Parameters (JSON):

{
  "table_name": "a1_2"
}

Required fields:

  • table_name: Name of the device table (e.g., "a1_2", "b3_1")

5) Sensor Configuration

Each mdm.measurement.device.sensor needs remotecontrol_params (JSON):

Required fields:

  • datetime_column: Column name for timestamp (usually "FECHA_HORA")
  • value_column: Column name for sensor value (e.g., "CAUDAL", "VOLUMEN", "PRESION")

Optional fields:

  • start_date: Initial sync date in YYYY-MM-DD format (default: last reading or current year start)

Example sensor configuration (Flow sensor):

{
  "datetime_column": "FECHA_HORA",
  "value_column": "CAUDAL",
  "start_date": "2025-01-01"
}

Another example (Volume sensor):

{
  "datetime_column": "FECHA_HORA",
  "value_column": "VOLUMEN"
}

Another example (Pressure sensor):

{
  "datetime_column": "FECHA_HORA",
  "value_column": "PRESION",
  "start_date": "2024-09-01"
}

6) SQL Query Example

For a flow sensor in device table "a1_2", the system generates:

SELECT ID_MEDIDA, FECHA_HORA, CAUDAL
FROM a1_2
WHERE FECHA_HORA >= '01/01/2025 00:00'
  AND FECHA_HORA <= '08/02/2026 23:59'
  AND CAUDAL IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY FECHA_HORA ASC

7) Export Table Schema

Before configuring sensors, export the database schema to understand available tables and columns:

  1. Execute action "SCADA Abaran New: Export table schema"
  2. Download CSV file from attachments
  3. Review available tables and their columns
  4. Use this information to configure device and sensor parameters

The CSV shows:

  • TABLE_NAME: Name of each table (use for device table_name)
  • COLUMN_NAME: Name of each column (use for datetime_column and value_column)
  • DATA_TYPE: SQL data type of the column
  • SAMPLE_VALUES: Example values from the first row

8) Get Devices Plan

Use action "SCADA Abaran New: Get devices (plan)" to build an execution plan:

  • Scans all configured devices and sensors
  • Determines date ranges to query for each sensor
  • Validates configuration parameters
  • Prepares the plan for the "Get readings" action

9) Get Readings

Use action "SCADA Abaran New: Get readings" to import sensor data:

  • Requires a plan from "Get devices (plan)" action
  • Queries each device table for configured sensors
  • Converts DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM format to UTC timestamps
  • Upserts readings into Odoo (no duplicates)
  • Creates detailed JSON audit attachment

10) Daily Sync Procedure

Run the procedure "SCADA Abaran New: Daily Sync" to automatically:

  1. Get devices plan
  2. Get readings for all sensors

This procedure can be scheduled to run daily via cron job.

11) Export Schema Procedure

Run the procedure "SCADA Abaran New: Export Schema" to export the database schema to CSV.

12) Technical Features

  • Native MariaDB Connection: Uses mysql-connector-python or pymysql (NOT ODBC)
  • Fixed Date Format: Always DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM (hardcoded, not configurable)
  • Timezone Conversion: Automatic Europe/Madrid → UTC conversion
  • UTF-8 Encoding: Full Unicode support with utf8mb4 charset
  • Per-Device Tables: Each device has its own table structure
  • Flexible Columns: Configurable datetime and value column names
  • CSV Schema Export: Generates complete database schema documentation
  • Audit Trail: Creates JSON attachments with detailed import results
  • Error Handling: Robust error handling with detailed error messages

13) Troubleshooting

  • Connection refused → Check host/port/firewall/VPN
  • Login failed → Verify credentials and database name
  • Driver not found → Install mysql-connector-python or pymysql
  • No data returned → Verify table_name, datetime_column, and value_column in configuration
  • Date parsing errors → Ensure database uses DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM format exactly
  • Encoding errors → Ensure charset is set to utf8mb4 in connection params
  • Table not found → Use "Export table schema" action to verify table names
  • Column not found → Use "Export table schema" action to verify column names
  • Empty CSV export → Check database connection and permissions
SCADA Abaran New: Export table schema

# Export table schema from SCADA Abaran New MariaDB database to CSV # Shows all tables and their columns with sample data import csv from io import BytesIO Remote = self.remote_id
# Connect to MariaDB database cursor = sql_connect() bag['_sql_cursor'] = cursor
try: # Get all tables in the database sql_execute(cursor, "SHOW TABLES", ()) tables = sql_fetchall(cursor)
# Create CSV in memory output = BytesIO() writer = csv.writer(output, delimiter=';', quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL)
# Write header writer.writerow([ 'TABLE_NAME', 'COLUMN_NAME', 'DATA_TYPE', 'SAMPLE_VALUES' ])
# For each table, get column information and sample data for table_row in tables: table_name = table_row[0]
# Skip system tables if table_name.startswith('_'): continue
# Get column information sql_execute(cursor, "DESCRIBE `%s`" % table_name, ()) columns = sql_fetchall(cursor)
# Get sample row try: sql_execute(cursor, "SELECT * FROM `%s` LIMIT 1" % table_name, ()) sample_row = sql_fetchone(cursor) except Exception: sample_row = None
# Write each column for idx, col_info in enumerate(columns): col_name = col_info[0] col_type = col_info[1] sample_value = ''
if sample_row and idx < len(sample_row) and sample_row[idx] is not None: sample_value = str(sample_row[idx])[:50] # Limit length
# Encode for Python 2.7 compatibility def encode_value(val): if val is None: return '' if isinstance(val, unicode): return val.encode('utf-8') return str(val)
writer.writerow([ encode_value(table_name), encode_value(col_name), encode_value(col_type), encode_value(sample_value) ])
# Get CSV content as bytes csv_bytes = output.getvalue() output.close()
# Create attachment attachment = env['ir.attachment'].create({ 'name': 'scada_abaran_new_schema_%s.csv' % ( fields.Datetime.now().replace(' ', '_').replace(':', '-') ), 'datas': base64.b64encode(csv_bytes), 'datas_fname': 'scada_abaran_new_schema.csv', 'res_model': 'remotecontrol', 'res_id': Remote.id, 'type': 'binary', })
result = "Exported database schema to CSV: %s" % attachment.name
finally: # Always close the connection cursor = bag.get('_sql_cursor') if cursor: sql_close(cursor)
bag['result'] = result

# Fetch readings from SCADA Abaran New MariaDB database and upsert into Odoo Remote = self.remote_id SensorModel = env['mdm.measurement.device.sensor'] plan = bag.get('sensors_plan') or []
if not plan: raise Exception("No sensors in plan. Run 'Get devices (plan)' first.")
final_date = fields.Date.today() initial_date = None total_upserts = 0 total_errors = 0 items = []
# Connect to SCADA database and store cursor in bag cursor = sql_connect() bag['_sql_cursor'] = cursor
try: for sensor_plan in plan: sensor_id = sensor_plan['sensor_id'] device_id = sensor_plan['device_id'] table_name = sensor_plan['table_name'] datetime_column = sensor_plan['datetime_column'] value_column = sensor_plan['value_column'] initial_date = sensor_plan['initial_date']
sensor_record = SensorModel.browse(sensor_id)
try: # Use ISO format for date filtering (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) # This works with both ISO and Spanish date formats in the database from datetime import datetime initial_dt = datetime.strptime(initial_date, '%Y-%m-%d') initial_str = initial_dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d 00:00:00')
# Final date with time final_dt = datetime.strptime(final_date, '%Y-%m-%d') final_str = final_dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d 23:59:59')
# Build query (without IS NOT NULL filter - allows 0 and NULL values) query = """ SELECT ID_MEDIDA, `%s`, `%s` FROM `%s` WHERE `%s` >= ? AND `%s` <= ? ORDER BY `%s` ASC """ % ( datetime_column, value_column, table_name, datetime_column, datetime_column, datetime_column )
query_params = ( initial_str, final_str )
sql_execute(cursor, query, query_params) rows = sql_fetchall(cursor)
upserts = 0 errs = 0 readings_summary = []
for row in rows: try: id_medida = row[0] fecha_hora_value = row[1] raw_value = float(row[2]) if row[2] is not None else 0.0
# Parse datetime - auto-detect format (ISO or Spanish) # Supported: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS[.mmm] or DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM[:SS] if hasattr(fecha_hora_value, 'strftime'): # It's already a datetime object naive_dt = fecha_hora_value else: # It's a string - auto-detect format fecha_str = str(fecha_hora_value).strip() naive_dt = None
# Try ISO formats first (YYYY-MM-DD) for fmt in ['%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f', '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M']: try: naive_dt = datetime.strptime(fecha_str, fmt) break except ValueError: continue
# Try Spanish formats (DD/MM/YYYY) if naive_dt is None: for fmt in ['%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S', '%d/%m/%Y %H:%M']: try: naive_dt = datetime.strptime(fecha_str, fmt) break except ValueError: continue
# If still not parsed, raise error if naive_dt is None: raise ValueError('Cannot parse date: %s' % fecha_str)
# Convert from Europe/Madrid to UTC madrid_tz = pytz.timezone('Europe/Madrid') local_dt = madrid_tz.localize(naive_dt) utc_dt = local_dt.astimezone(pytz.UTC) timestamp = fields.Datetime.to_string(utc_dt.replace(tzinfo=None))
# Upsert reading into Odoo Remote.upsert( 'mdm.measurement.device.sensor.reading', { 'sensor_id': sensor_record.id, 'measurement_time': timestamp }, { 'value': raw_value, 'remotecontrol_origin_id': Remote.id } ) upserts += 1
# Keep sample for audit (limit to first 10) if len(readings_summary) < 10: readings_summary.append({ 'id_medida': id_medida, 'fecha_hora_original': str(fecha_hora_value), 'time_utc': timestamp, 'value': raw_value })
except Exception as e: errs += 1 if len(readings_summary) < 10: readings_summary.append({ 'row': str(row), 'error': str(e) })
total_upserts += upserts total_errors += errs
items.append({ 'sensor_id': sensor_id, 'device_id': device_id, 'table_name': table_name, 'datetime_column': datetime_column, 'value_column': value_column, 'status': 'success', 'points_found': len(rows), 'upserts': upserts, 'errors': errs, 'readings': readings_summary })
except Exception as e: total_errors += 1 items.append({ 'sensor_id': sensor_id, 'device_id': device_id, 'table_name': table_name, 'datetime_column': datetime_column, 'value_column': value_column, 'status': 'error', 'error': str(e) })
finally: # Always close the connection cursor = bag.get('_sql_cursor') if cursor: sql_close(cursor)
# Create audit attachment audit = { 'executed_at': str(fields.Datetime.now()), 'initial_date': initial_date if plan else None, 'final_date': final_date, 'total_upserts': total_upserts, 'total_errors': total_errors, 'sensors_processed': len(plan), 'items': items }
try: audit_json = json.dumps(audit, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2, default=str) b64 = base64.b64encode(audit_json.encode('utf-8')) except Exception as json_error: simple_audit = { 'executed_at': str(fields.Datetime.now()), 'total_upserts': total_upserts, 'total_errors': total_errors, 'error': str(json_error) } audit_json = json.dumps(simple_audit, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2) b64 = base64.b64encode(audit_json.encode('utf-8'))
fname = 'scada_abaran_new_readings_%s.json' % ( fields.Datetime.now().replace(':', '').replace('-', '').replace(' ', '_') )
att = env['ir.attachment'].create({ 'name': fname, 'datas_fname': fname, 'datas': b64, 'mimetype': 'application/json', 'res_model': 'remotecontrol', 'res_id': Remote.id })
Remote.message_post( body="[SCADA Abaran New Readings] upserts=%s errors=%s sensors=%s" % ( total_upserts, total_errors, len(plan) ), attachment_ids=[att.id] )
bag['upserts'] = total_upserts bag['errors'] = total_errors bag['audit_attachment_id'] = att.id
